facts.subject: Cheaping Knowe
facts.statement: Lawful wives, guarded damsels and concubine slaves dare not look at men; other women may befriend strangers.

refs.q: such women as were wedded according to law, or damsels in the care of their kindred, or slaves who were concubines, had not dared so much as to look on a man

facts.subject: (unnamed) thrall-market stone
facts.statement: Thralls are bid on like horses; buyers strip them in the booth to check for damage; hansel is paid at sale.

refs.q: most of them before they bid their highest had the chattels away into the merchant's booth to strip them

facts.subject: (unnamed) thrall-market stone
facts.statement: Thirteen chattels sold in one session, four young women among them.

refs.q: There was a half score and three of these chattels to be sold

A feared regional tyrant whom merchants will not name, as an antagonist faction.

ledger.summary: In Cheaping Knowe married women, guarded damsels and concubine slaves may not look at men. On the fourth day Clement takes Ralph to the thrall-market, where a black-bearded merchant in scarlet sells thirteen captives from a stone after buyers inspect them stripped. Privately the merchant says Bull Nosy brought the damsel but she was too proud to sell, refusing to be stripped, so he led her away (she riding, he on foot, since mountain men are no horsemen), probably to Whiteness to give or sell her to the dreaded Lord of Utterbol. Clement calls Utterbol the worst and perhaps mightiest tyrant of these lands.
ledger.geography_notes: Whiteness is a town on the company's road beyond Cheaping Knowe, where the Lord of Utterbol may be met. Utterbol is the lord's domain (location not given).
